data.name: Ampika
data.gender_notes: Ampika is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word 'ampu' meaning delight and 'pika' meaning love, pleasure or pleasing. This name is associated with the goddess Durga and represents the feminine qualities of love, compassion and delight. The name Ampika carries the meaning “Delight, Love, Pleasing” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Ampika usually hope their child will grow to embody delight, love, pleasing and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the divine feminine and the power of love and compassion.
data.etymology: Ampika belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Delight, Love, Pleasing.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ampika total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The name Ampika is rooted in Indian mythology and holds deep cultural significance in Hindu beliefs. It is a beautiful and expressive name indicative of joy, pleasure and love, which resonates with the character traits valued in Hindu culture. It is also a reminder of the goddess Durga, who embodies the feminine power, love and compassion in Hindu teachings.
data.spiritual_significance: In a spiritual context, the name Ampika symbolizes the divine feminine energy of love, compassion, and delight. It reminds us of the power of these qualities and encourages us to cultivate them within ourselves. The name also serves as a connection to the goddess Durga, who represents the supreme power and protector of all. By carrying this name, one can evoke the blessings and guidance of this powerful deity.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Ampika: Goddess of fertility and prosperity. Symbolizes the nurturing and abundant energy of Mother Earth, fostering growth and abundance in all aspects of life.

historical_references.reference: The Mahabharata mentions a woman named Ampika, daughter of the king of Madra named Sisupala. She was married to Bhishma, the grandsire of the Pandavas. Once, during a hunting expedition, Bhishma saw Ampika bathing in a lake. Unable to control his lust, he approached her, but she rebuffed him. Infuriated, Bhishma cursed her to be a leper for life.
historical_references.context: An episode from the epic Mahabharata

historical_references.reference: Another reference to Ampika is found in the Puranas, where she is described as the mother of the god Indra. In one version of the story, when Indra was a baby, he was taken care of by a she-demon named Tushtima. Tushtima fell in love with Indra and tried to keep him from his parents. When Indra grew up, he killed Tushtima. Ampika, who was heartbroken at the loss of her foster-mother, cursed Indra to be defeated in battle by a woman.
historical_references.context: A story from the Hindu Puranas
